stem: (Select TWO.) Marlowe Freight packages one module as a single file in an AWS object-storage bucket. Later an engineer edits the address in the `module` block to point at a newer file. Which two statements about this setup are accurate?

choices.text: A source that points at a plain folder of loose `.tf` objects works the same way as one that points at a packaged file
The object has to be an archive, for example a `.zip` or `.tar.gz` file
The address can use the three-part `<NAMESPACE>/<NAME>/<PROVIDER>` shape, with the bucket name as the namespace
The new file is picked up only after the `.terraform` directory has been deleted and recreated
After the edit, `terraform init` has to run again before the new code is installed

rationale: For an S3 source the object must be an archive, and the address uses the `s3::` prefix. Changing the `source` argument requires another `terraform init`, because modules are installed at initialization. Loose `.tf` objects are not a supported shape for this kind of source, which expects one archive object. The three-part `NAMESPACE/NAME/PROVIDER` shape is a registry address, while a bucket object is addressed with the `s3::` prefix. Nothing requires deleting the `.terraform` directory: re-running init after the edit is what installs the new code.
